summary:
In deep-space missions to the Moon and Mars, communication delays of up to 22 minutes mean astronauts cannot wait for doctors on Earth during a medical emergency. Contistellaria Health developed RIG-3D, an autonomous, Offline-First biomedical operating system designed for spacecraft, space stations, rovers, and planetary bases. 

RIG-3D addresses all 5 NASA Human Research Program (HRP) hazards (Radiation, Isolation, Distance, Gravity fields, and Hostile closed environments) through four integrated modules:
1. A 3D Holographic Body Scanner paired with a diegetic 10-LED spinal rail (DRI) for instant visual triage (Cyan, Amber, Red) and closed-loop suit regulation (automated CO2 helmet purging with +20% O2 and LCVG liquid cooling).
2. Real-time Crew Telemetry for 5 officers, 6 dynamic vital-sign trends, manual keyboard triage, and local CSV/Excel clinical export.
3. AR Helmet Camera optical scanning (rPPG pulse and blink fatigue) plus step-by-step guided microgravity ultrasound (ONSD/SANS, cardiac, femoral).
4. Crew wellness gamification (XP missions) and an emergency color guide.

Live Demo: https://astronaut-health-mon-g5w5.bolt.host/

1. What does it do and how does it work?

RIG-3D (by Contistellaria Health) is an autonomous, Offline-First biomedical operating system designed for deep-space missions across 4 operational environments: Spacecraft (1.3s delay), Space Station (0.8s delay), Lunar/Martian Rover (14 min delay), and Planetary Base (22 min delay). Instead of acting as a passive monitor that waits for Earth, RIG-3D operates as a closed-loop medical guardian through 4 modules:

- Module 1 (3D Holographic Body Scanner & 5 NASA HRP Risks): Monitors cranial, airway, cardiovascular, spinal, abdominal, and lower-extremity nodes alongside a 10-LED spinal rail (DRI). When a crisis occurs (such as EVA helmet CO2 buildup or hypoxia), the system automatically executes suit countermeasures (+20% O2 purge, 10°C LCVG liquid cooling, and LBNP negative pressure) with offline voice synthesis.

- Module 2 (Crew Telemetry & Self-Evaluation): Tracks basal biomarkers for all 5 mission officers (Carlos Junior, Jairo Pachas, Christian Degregori, Carlos Huamani, and Anthony Salcedo), renders 6 dynamic vital-sign trends (Sol 1 to Sol 7), provides keyboard triage input, and exports local CSV/Excel clinical reports.

- Module 3 (AR Helmet Camera & Guided Ultrasound): Uses optical webcam scanning (rPPG pulse and blink rate) to detect circadian fatigue and provides 3-step guided ultrasound instructions (Ocular ONSD for SANS, Cardiac, and Femoral bone integrity) for non-medical astronauts.

- Module 4 (Gamification & Emergency Color Guide): Motivates daily ARED exercise, hydration, and circadian routines through an XP readiness bar and a Cyan/Amber/Red triage protocol guide.

2. What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact?

In Mars or lunar surface excursions, a 22-minute radio delay makes real-time telemedicine from Houston impossible during acute hypoxia, hypercapnia, or intracranial pressure spikes (SANS). RIG-3D empowers astronauts—even without surgical training—to diagnose conditions in under one second and stabilizes their vital signs autonomously. It is designed to integrate directly into next-generation spacesuits (such as the Axiom AxEMU LCVG/HUD architecture and Astroskin biometric garments).

3. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did we use?

- Software & Languages: React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Vite, Lucide Icons, HTML5 SVG 3D holographic rendering.

- Browser & Offline APIs: Web Speech API (SpeechSynthesis for offline suit voice alerts), WebRTC MediaDevices API (live AR helmet camera feed), and local Blob CSV/Excel file storage generation.

- Target Hardware: Cabin tablets, webcam/optical helmet sensors, and spacesuit PLSS/HUD interfaces.
